title: Analytical / Precision Balance

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)
Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: Measures mass with high precision, used for weighing reagents and media components, especially for small quantities where accuracy matters most.
operatingPrinciple: An electronic load cell converts the force from the sample's weight into an electrical signal proportional to mass, typically to a precision of milligrams or better for analytical-grade balances.
basicOperation: Level the balance and allow it to warm up/stabilize per manufacturer guidance before use.
Tare with the empty weighing vessel in place.
Add material slowly, especially for fine powders, and record the stable reading.
importantSettings: Draft shield/door position (open doors introduce air currents that destabilize readings on sensitive balances).
calibration: Periodic calibration with certified calibration weights per facility schedule; many balances also support internal auto-calibration routines.
maintenance: Keep the weighing pan and chamber clean of spilled material.
Avoid moving the balance, which can affect its level/calibration.

commonErrors.cause: Draft, vibration, an unlevel balance, or static on a plastic weigh boat
commonErrors.fix: Close draft shield doors, ensure a stable/level surface, and use an anti-static measure for plastic weigh boats if needed

safety: Follow the safety data sheet for any hazardous reagent being weighed.
